newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch call rates stay down ahead of new quota.
newsitem.headline: Dutch call rates stay down ahead of new quota.

text.p: Dutch overnight money continued to trade below its customary levels, still affected by an excess of liquidity ahead of Friday's expiry of the three-month secured loans quota.
Call was quoted virtually unchanged from Tuesday, changing hands between 2.38 and 2.50 percent.
"Like yesterday, there's a lot of liquidity. Call will remain at these levels until the new quota," one dealer said.
"People are using up what they have left under the expiring quota," another said.
Traders agreed call money would regain higher levels at the start of the new quota. "It will be back near 3.00, 3.13 percent on Friday," one dealer said.
He said rates of one- to three- month deposits were also likely to edge up on Friday.
One-month deposits quoted at 3.06/14 percent bid/ask, slightly down from Tuesday.
Trade was extremely calm, focusing on overnight money and the very short deposits, dealers said. They noticed no particular activity in Dutch Treasury Certificates.
This morning, the Dutch central bank adjusted the size of the secured loans quota and of the cash reserve requirement set yesterday and effective from this Friday.
The compulsory cash reserve requirement running to April 29 was revised upward to 5.80 billion guilders from the 5.65 billion guilders announced yesterday.
Dealers said the changes had no impact on trade.
The guilder fractionally strengthened against the mark, trading at 112.352 per 100 marks from 112.395 on Tuesday.
